facts.statement: Gyposaurus is a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of South Africa whose name means "vulture lizard".
facts.quote: Gyposaurus (meaning "vulture lizard", referring to the outdated hypothesis that prosauropods were carnivores) is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the early Jurassic of South Africa.

facts.statement: The species Gyposaurus capensis was named in 1911 by Robert Broom based on a partial skeleton found in the Upper Elliot Formation of Orange Free State, South Africa.
facts.quote: G. capensis was named in 1911 by Scottish physician and paleontologist Robert Broom from a partial skeleton consisting of eleven dorsal and six caudal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, partial right scapula, right pelvic girdle, left ilium, and most of the right leg, discovered in the Upper Elliot Formation of Orange Free State, South Africa.

facts.statement: Robert Broom originally assigned the specimen of Gyposaurus capensis to the dubious genus Hortalotarsus.
facts.quote: Originally, he thought the specimen belonged to the dubious genus Hortalotarsus.

facts.statement: Michael Cooper synonymized Gyposaurus capensis with Massospondylus in 1981, a classification that has been generally accepted.
facts.quote: Galton and Cluver placed it in the genus Anchisaurus in 1976, but Michael Cooper synonymized it with Massospondylus in 1981, which has been generally accepted.

facts.statement: The species Gyposaurus sinensis was named in 1941 by Yang Zhongjian based on four specimens from the Early Jurassic Lufeng Formation of Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: "G." sinensis was named by Yang Zhongjian (C.C. Young) in 1941 for four specimens including jaw fragments and postcranial material from the Early Jurassic Lufeng Formation of Yunnan Province, China.

facts.statement: Galton referred Gyposaurus sinensis to Lufengosaurus in 1976, while Dong Zhiming referred it to Anchisaurus in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1976, Galton referred it to Lufengosaurus, while Dong Zhiming referred it to Anchisaurus in 1992.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Gyposaurus sinensis is a valid species or a junior synonym of Lufengosaurus huenei, as some referred specimens require further study.
facts.quote: Unpublished results of a presentation by Wang and colleagues at the SVP 2017 conference indicate that "G." sinensis is a junior synonym of Lufengosaurus huenei; however, some referred specimens need further study to determine their relationships.

facts.statement: Gyposaurus lived approximately 195 million years ago during the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) in what is now Africa and Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 195 millones de años, en el Sinemuriano, en lo que es hoy África y Asia.

facts.statement: Gyposaurus is usually considered to represent juveniles of other prosauropods, though G. sinensis is possibly a valid species.
facts.quote: Usualmente es considerado un juvenil de otros prosaurópodos, pero G. sinensis es posiblemente una especie válida según la última revisión de Prosauropoda de Galton y Upchurch en 2004.

facts.statement: The parent group of Gyposaurus is Anchisauridae.
Gyposaurus lived from the Hettangian to the Toarcian stages, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Toarcian (201.4 to 174.7 million years ago)
